distinction: thin straight parallel stripes of strong contrast
positive: zebra, picket fence, typewriter keys, clock hand, stripes on a sleeve, safety pin

distinction: Is the local pattern fine parallel stripes or thin lines at one slant, or broad shapes? Fine slanted stripes push up.
positive: fine dark and light stripes and hairlines (striped shirts, zebra, bicycle spokes, wheel fork, clock hand, handlebar), mostly one slant
negative: wide thick bars and big curved bands (wheel rims, window frames, blinds) at the other orientations

distinction: a vivid saturated colour patch that differs strongly from the colours around it
positive: purple, magenta, yellow and blue patches: toy, bottle, pretzel, anemone, parrot, mask
negative: not read (neg sheet not looked at)

distinction: Is there a single dark round disc (pupil, polka dot, hole) in a lighter surround, bigger than s2:71's dot? Big dark discs push up.
positive: single dark round discs: cat pupil, polka dots, a sign circle, tomato slice hole, totem hole, trigger buttons, wheel hubs

distinction: Is the stripe pitch very fine (one or two pixels) and parallel, or wide? Fine parallel stripes push up strongly.
positive: the finest parallel stripe patterns at any slant: zebra, vacuum hose coils, accordion, honeycomb ridges, fire engine slats, bikini edge
negative: wider stripes (striped shirts), text and rings at normal pitch

distinction: a small round saturated blob sitting on a contrasting ground
positive: berries, tomatoes, red dots on a joystick, balls, ladybug, strawberry on cream

distinction: a single tall or sky-backed structure against a furry eyed face
positive: towers, lighthouses, chimneys, airship, umbrella on open sky; also two dog photos
negative: dog faces plus one fox face and one human face; keeps out faces

distinction: Is there a bold bright vertical or slanted bar on a dark ground, or a thin ring or hairline? Bold bars push up, thin curved lines push down (large negative values).
positive: bold bright strokes on dark: thick letters (Model T, DEAD), tow truck stripes, clock numerals, neon letters
negative: very strong negative on thin ring outlines and hairlines (rings, ruler ticks, gown seam, neon thin lines)

distinction: a round wheel set in a long smooth painted body (side view of a vehicle) against a soft centered face or radial bloom with a dark nose or eye-like middle
positive: side views of vans, fire engines, cabs, a go-kart: wheel plus flat body panel; top 16 are all vehicles with a visible wheel
negative: human and dog faces (nose, mouth), daisies and other flowers with a round centre; keeps out faces and radial organic shapes

distinction: a smooth empty field with a thin edge object entering at its border
positive: plain blue sky or plain background, with a pole, wire, shaker or hull entering at an edge

distinction: thin dark straight lines that cross at an angle over a pale, bright ground
positive: bare twigs on sky, wires, music stand, chrome rim, panel edges, car roof edge, pan rim
negative: not read (stage 2 here: crops are tiny)

distinction: Detects printed letters, digits and marks on a surface.
positive: Text and logos on laptop, phone, odometer, book jacket, helmet, digital clock.

distinction: Is there a dark patch or heavy letter on white, or a smooth gradient? Dark bold patches on white push up.
positive: dark heavy letters and dots on white or pale ground (PHP, Cheese, dots on a lighter, bird silhouettes)
negative: smooth gradients and soft edges, fur, dark-to-light shaded surfaces

distinction: Detects four-legged body seen from the side on a ground.
positive: Dogs on lawn: Leonberg, Rottweiler, collie, wild boar, bear, dingo, rat, dowitchers with legs in view.

distinction: Is the patch dark with a hard corner against light, or a small round spot? Large dark flat areas push up weakly.
positive: large dark flat regions with a hard edge: black clothing, tyre, dark panels, wheel well
negative: small round dark holes and dots on white (pen dots, skull eyes, bead holes, boat windows)

distinction: Saturated orange or yellow patch.
positive: Macaw, bell pepper, lemon, sarong, king penguin patch.
negative: Dog faces and screens, at very low strength (-.5).

distinction: Is there a dark curved band across lighter bumpy or mixed texture? Weak. Mid-width curved bands push up.
positive: mixed texture with a curved dark band: honeycomb cells, bicycle brake cable, apples, goblet letters, blue chair bars

distinction: Head with two upright pointed ears on a front face.
positive: Collie, Australian terrier, Groenendael, Eskimo dog, hyena, toy terrier.

distinction: a narrow tip or neck that tapers up from a wider body, standing upright
positive: bottle necks, spires, shaker caps, baby bottle teats, stupa, bell tower tops

distinction: Is there a small dark round dot on a plain light ground, or a thin dark stroke? Dot pushes up, thin stroke pushes down.
positive: isolated small dark dots and round holes on light ground: eyes, skull sockets, pen dots, punctuation, bold letter blobs
negative: thin dark strokes and hairlines on light ground (script writing, twigs, clock hands): the opposite of a dot is a line

distinction: Detects long thin edges lying across a plain ground, like feathers, spokes or ties.
positive: Wing feathers, cart wheel, bow tie, pineapple scales, tail, knife blade.

distinction: Is there a short bright outline stroke or edge, or a long straight line? Short curved outline strokes push up, long straight lines push down.
positive: thin bright outlines of letters, logos and rims, repeated small stripes (zebra, mesh): many short edges close together
negative: long straight smooth lines crossing the crop (rails, wires, bars) and big rings at low contrast

distinction: Detects a small pale blob on a darker area, near a dark edge.
positive: White paws, ping-pong ball, pale muzzle, dalmatian spot, candle flame, white feet of dogs.

distinction: Detects dark patches scattered on a lighter ground.
positive: Dalmatian, setter, ladybug, snake skin, goose bill, Doberman, Rottweiler tan marks, mantis.

distinction: Pale cream face of a dog or sheep.
positive: Labrador, Saluki, whippet, dalmatian, bighorn, Great Pyrenees faces.

distinction: Warm dark silhouette shapes with sharp steps against a glow.
positive: Staircase, throne bust, pier railing, drilling platform at dusk, honeycomb.

distinction: Are there many dense horizontal parallel bars (louvres, grille slats)? Dense horizontal bars push up.
positive: dense horizontal bars and ridges: grille, vent slats, accordion, coils, striped shirt, steam locomotive grille
negative: not read (sheet made, no image opened)

distinction: Thin lines fanning out from a centre, versus dense dark bristle with a centre.
positive: Bolo tie, daisy petals, fan feathers, wheel spokes, a dome from below.
negative: Dense bristles: daisy centre, echidna, porcupine, Pomeranian face, macaque.

distinction: a small round or lettered mark on a smooth ground against fine irregular fur or mesh
positive: hub caps, letters, dials, eyes of birds: small bold mark on smooth ground
negative: fur, chainlink fence, honeycomb, hair, moss: dense fine irregular texture; keeps out fine texture

distinction: Fine regular ridges and ribs wound around.
positive: Brain coral, ammonite, hose ribs, snake scales, baseball seams, typewriter bar.

distinction: Is there a tiny isolated dark dot (eye, hole, screw), or something else? Tiny dark dots on a lighter surface push up.
positive: tiny isolated dark dots on a lighter surface: eye of bird or cockatoo, screw holes, puck, dalmatian spots, pen dots, flying birds far away

distinction: Is there a small round ring or dot with an outline (a screw, a circled mark), or a straight thin line? Small rings push up (to 14), straight lines push down (to -12).
positive: small closed round outlines: circled (c), knob rings, screws, coins, round buttons, mushroom spots, neon circles
negative: long straight thin lines and strokes: spokes, hands, bridge wires, thin edges. Strong, -12.

distinction: a smooth blank surface or soft blur against a furry face with eyes
positive: plain wall, painted car side, bib, perfume bottle, blurred feathers: low-texture areas; also two dog close-ups with grey fur
negative: frontal dog faces and a gibbon face; keeps out furry eyed faces

distinction: Smooth narrow front face with a dark nose, versus fluffy-ruffed face.
positive: Dingo, toy terrier, red wolf, whippet, Doberman, Great Pyrenees front face.
negative: Ruffed faces: collie, papillon, Pomeranian, Eskimo dog, gibbon.

distinction: Is the patch saturated green, or any other colour? Pure bright green pushes this channel strongly down; other colours push it up weakly.
positive: weak: neutral or warm surfaces with edges (gray, tan, clock face, text)
negative: saturated green of any shape: green lights, vine, green umbrella, beetle, green kitchen items

distinction: a pointed pair of ears over a narrow muzzle, facing the viewer
positive: dog, fox, wolf, collie faces; a Polaroid camera front

distinction: Is there a small bright spot in the dark, or a flat uniform area? Bright spots on black push up.
positive: small bright lights and bright letters on black: stage lights, candle, sparks, street lights, white text on black
negative: flat uniform surfaces: grey wall, dark cloth, soft shadow gradient, the bottom border

distinction: Detects a plain smooth sky or ground with the edge of an object at the side.
positive: Tops of towers, mountains, crane, mast, a dog head cut off at the corner on a blue sky.

distinction: a small round or lettered mark on a smooth ground against fine irregular fur or mesh
positive: hub caps, letters, dials, eyes of birds: small bold mark on smooth ground
negative: fur, chainlink fence, honeycomb, hair, moss: dense fine irregular texture; keeps out fine texture

distinction: Is the patch a smooth broad surface (curved, plain, shaded) or small bold print? Smooth surfaces push up, bold print and rings push down.
positive: smooth broad coloured surfaces and gentle curves: fig, pumpkin, camera barrel, loafer, red paper, thimble, clothing
negative: bold print and ring patterns: rings on cloth, lettering, keyboard keys, remote buttons, dials

distinction: a repeated small pattern (scales, dots, keys, bands) against a furry face
positive: snake skin, accordion keys, ladybug, spider, keypad: regular repeated marks
negative: dog and monkey faces (z -5.1, deepest of the set); keeps out faces

distinction: Is there a thin curved arc or rim, or a filled round disc? Thin round rims push up, filled discs and soft round shapes push down.
positive: thin curved rims and arcs: bicycle wheels, bucket handle, wheel rims, brake lights, domes, eye rims, French horn tube
negative: filled soft round discs and plates: paper lanterns, CD, plates, round buttons, sea slug blob, bobsled helmet

distinction: Detects a saturated pink or bright colour patch.
positive: Pink umbrella, jellyfish, lotion, handkerchief, picks, parachute, patterned skirt.

distinction: a narrow shape that tapers into a pale or open region at the edge of the view
positive: dog snouts at the frame edge, flute, bridge arches, tower, camera barrel, scooter handle, croquet hoop

distinction: Is there a very fine bright curl, tooth or stripe, or a round ring? Fine curls and teeth push up, rings and discs push down.
positive: finest repeated bright lines and teeth: zebra stripes, comb teeth, wing feather tips, logo curls, game-pad symbols
negative: round rings, circles and discs (keyboard keys, joystick dots, owl eye, bold letters)

distinction: Is there a thick bold stroke (heavy letters), or a ring or fine zebra stripe? Heavy strokes push up.
positive: heavy bold lettering and thick dark bars on a plain ground (Yale, Marc, BARB, 110 numerals)
negative: rings, circled marks, zebra stripes, wheel rims, honeycomb thin walls: thin repeated structure

distinction: Are there thin separate lines or wires meeting at an angle, or dense regular ridges? Thin lines at junctions push up, dense ridges push down.
positive: thin separate edges forming junctions: chain-link fence, violin strings, clock hands, wire harness, buckle, ruler corner, kite wing feathers
negative: dense regular ridges: vacuum hose coils, typewriter ridges, compass ticks, ruler marks, honeycomb, comb teeth

distinction: Is there a bold broad stroke, or fine repeated stripes? Bold strokes push up (weakly), fine periodic stripes push down.
positive: bold broad strokes and shapes: letters, skull, wheel spokes, keys, wide stripes
negative: dense fine periodic stripes (zebra, spider web, wrapped cord, iris threads): the pitch is too fine

distinction: a bold painted body part with a glossy curve (wheel arch, grille, lens) against a plain flat thing
positive: vehicle fronts, wheels, grilles, tractors, pinwheel; paint on curved metal
negative: street sign, space bar, telephone, one dog nose: plain flat or thin-lined man-made things

distinction: a smooth round rim or disc on a flat glossy surface
positive: wheels of vans, rims of cups, bottle necks, joystick: round smooth edge on plain surface

distinction: Detects a small pale blob on a darker area, near a dark edge.
positive: White paws, ping-pong ball, pale muzzle, dalmatian spot, candle flame, white feet of dogs.

distinction: Small hard-edged dark-and-light hardware detail.
positive: Locomotive window band, telephone dial, padlock, tandem frame, photocopier panel.

distinction: a cluster of small round or oval bumps packed together
positive: olives, peas, lemons in a bowl, daisy centre, brain coral, knotted rope, pom-poms

distinction: Detects a plain smooth sky or ground with the edge of an object at the side.
positive: Tops of towers, mountains, crane, mast, a dog head cut off at the corner on a blue sky.

distinction: Warm saturated orange-red glossy surface.
positive: Fig, stew, agaric, crab, egg yolk, car window glare.

distinction: soft organic bloom or fur patch (radial or furry mass) against the man-made channels' side
positive: dog nose, gibbon, thistle, daisy, sunflower pictures, pelican bill: furry or petal mass, not cars

distinction: White surface, versus blue sky and hard-edged man-made things.
positive: White poodle, Samoyed, Saluki, egg, vulture head, white blossom.
negative: Blue sky scenes: lighthouse, planetarium, alp, castle, radio telescope.

distinction: Not read: its sheet was made, not opened.
positive: Not read.

distinction: long thin blades or stalks laid across a darker textured ground
positive: grass and leaf blades, snake over leaves, fur whiskers, mushroom stem, flute

distinction: Rounded curved warm brown or metal body parts in close crop.
positive: Trombone, throne post, bull mastiff legs, brass finial, weasel fur.

distinction: tight parallel ridges that curve (coil, bellows, fan) against straight dense lines
positive: typewriter, spring, hose, fan palm, fish fin, accordion: curved ribs
negative: compass dial, mesh, striped sock, blinds: straight dense lines or grids

distinction: Detects dark patches scattered on a lighter ground.
positive: Dalmatian, setter, ladybug, snake skin, goose bill, Doberman, Rottweiler tan marks, mantis.

distinction: Flat blank sky or bright smooth field.
positive: Blue sky, white sky, plain background.

distinction: Thin straight lines against a contrasting field.
positive: Guitar strings, spokes, piano keys, wing feathers, leopard whiskers.

distinction: Fine check or woven pattern on a body, against plain.
positive: Plaid shirts, gingham, toaster, rugby ball, newt, fur: small repeated texture.

distinction: Detects a pointed-ear head with tan muzzle facing the camera.
positive: Dingo, cairn, red fox, dhole, red wolf, gazelle, impala, basset, beagle, lesser panda.
